intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

selected_hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Arrive early afternoon to maximize Day 1. Walk through Staré Město (Old Town), witness the medieval Astronomical Clock strike the hour, and explore the Gothic Týn Church. Stay centrally at a hotel within walking distance of Old Town Square to avoid transit delays after your adjusted early-afternoon flight arrival. A guided 2-hour walking tour covers Josefov (Jewish Quarter) and Charles Bridge at golden hour.

experiences.name: Czech Food & Beer Tasting in Vinohrady
experiences.description: Skip tourist-trap restaurants near the castle and head to Vinohrady, a residential neighborhood beloved by locals. Join a 3-hour food tour sampling svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce), trdelník, and craft Bohemian lagers at authentic pubs. Staying in Vinohrady or Žižkov keeps you steps from the best local eateries and reduces commute time, making this ideal for Day 2 or 3.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl & Street Food Night
experiences.description: After the train or bus hop from Prague to Budapest (Day 4–5), base yourself in the Jewish Quarter (District VII) — the heart of Budapest's nightlife and ruin bar scene. Explore Szimpla Kert and neighboring bars while sampling lángos (deep-fried dough), kürtőskalács, and chimney cake from street vendors. Staying in District VII or V puts you within a 5-minute walk of all major stops.

experiences.name: Budapest Castle Hill & Matthias Church Exploration
experiences.description: Dedicate a morning to Buda Castle Hill, home to the Royal Palace, Matthias Church, and Fisherman's Bastion with panoramic views over the Danube. Book a hotel in District I (Castle Hill) or District V (Belváros) to walk up or take the historic funicular. Arrive by 09:00 to beat crowds. Includes entry to Matthias Church and the Hungarian National Gallery.

experiences.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath Experience
experiences.description: A quintessential Budapest activity. The iconic Széchenyi Baths in City Park (District XIV) offer outdoor and indoor thermal pools steeped in 19th-century grandeur. Book a hotel in District VI (Terézváros) or District VII to be within a 15-minute walk or short metro ride. Visit on Day 6 or 7 as a relaxing cultural wind-down. Entry includes locker and towel rental.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight lands at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use the time to collect luggage, take the airport bus (Line 119 to Nádraží Veleslavín, then Metro Line A to Staroměstská) for ~60 CZK, and check into your boutique stay in Staré Město.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Town Orientation Walk: After dropping your bags, take a self-guided walk through Staré Město. Stroll across Charles Bridge (free), admire the Gothic towers, and explore the Old Town Square to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) — watch the hourly show for free. Pop into Týn Church courtyard and soak in the medieval atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Wenceslas Square & Národní Třída: Take a leisurely evening walk down Wenceslas Square, a historic boulevard lined with architecture and buzzing with locals. Stop at the National Museum steps for a great photo. Return to Old Town for dinner in a side-street local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry (trdelník or chlebíček open-faced sandwich) from a bakery near the airport or at the metro station — budget ~80 CZK.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick street food bite near Old Town Square — try a sausage (klobása) from a street vendor for ~60–80 CZK.
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33) — a beloved Czech pub with affordable traditional dishes like svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or smažený sýr (fried cheese). Budget ~250–350 CZK including a Pilsner Urquell draft beer.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 24-hour transit pass (120 CZK) from the airport — it covers all buses, trams, and metro for the rest of the day. September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C), so a light jacket for the evening is recommended. Exchange a small amount of cash to CZK; avoid airport exchange booths — use a Revolut card or ATM in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Prague Castle Complex: Take Tram 22 from Náměstí Republiky up to Pražský hrad (Prague Castle). Explore the castle grounds, St. Vitus Cathedral (exterior free, interior with ticket ~250 CZK), Golden Lane (a charming row of tiny historic houses), and enjoy panoramic views over the red rooftops of Prague. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Malá Strana (Lesser Town) Exploration: Walk downhill from the castle through the picturesque Malá Strana district. Visit the Baroque St. Nicholas Church (75 CZK), wander cobblestone lanes, and discover hidden courtyards. Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore its statues and street artists at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Josefov (Jewish Quarter) Evening Stroll: Walk through the historic Jewish Quarter — the exteriors of the synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery are free to admire from the outside. The area is atmospheric and quiet in the evening. End the night with a beer at a local pub.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre (Národní 22) — a classic Prague café with affordable breakfast sets (eggs, bread, coffee) for ~150–200 CZK. A historic spot beloved by locals.
meals.lunch: Grab a hearty lunch at a local jídelna (canteen-style Czech diner) near Malá Strana — look for daily lunch specials (denní menu) which include soup + main course for ~150–180 CZK.
meals.dinner: Pivovarský Klub (Křižíkova 17, Žižkov) — a craft beer pub with excellent Czech food. Try the roast pork knee (vepřové koleno) or goulash. Budget ~280–380 CZK with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: The Prague Castle circuit tickets range from 250–350 CZK depending on which route you choose. Route B (St. Vitus Cathedral + Old Royal Palace + St. George's Basilica + Golden Lane) is the best value. Buy a 3-day transit pass (330 CZK) today to cover the next three days of travel in Prague.

day_by_day.morning: Vyšehrad Fortress: Take Metro Line C to Vyšehrad station and explore this lesser-visited but stunning hilltop fortress. Walk the ramparts for free, visit the Romanesque Rotunda of St. Martin (free exterior), and stroll through the Vyšehrad Cemetery where famous Czech figures like Dvořák and Mucha are buried (free entry). Incredible views of the Vltava River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Vinohrady & Žižkov Neighborhoods: Head to the bohemian Žižkov district — visit the iconic Žižkov Television Tower (observation deck ~250 CZK) with its famous crawling baby sculptures by David Černý. Walk through the hip Vinohrady neighborhood, browsing local shops and cafés. Visit the Church of the Most Sacred Heart of Our Lord — a striking Art Deco-Modernist church (free).
day_by_day.evening: Náplavka Riverbank: Head to the Náplavka embankment along the Vltava River, a favorite local hangout spot. In September there are often evening markets and food stalls. Grab a beer from a riverside kiosk and watch the sun set over the city.

meals.breakfast: Eska Bakery (Pernerova 49, Karlín) — one of Prague's best artisan bakeries. Fresh sourdough, pastries, and excellent coffee for ~120–160 CZK.
meals.lunch: Manifesto Market (Náplavka area) or a local kebab/falafel shop in Žižkov — budget street food for ~100–150 CZK.
meals.dinner: Náplavka riverside food stalls or a nearby local restaurant in Vinohrady. Try Café Slávia (Smetanovo nábřeží 2) for affordable Czech classics with a river view — budget ~250–320 CZK.

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is completely free to enter and is far less crowded than Prague Castle — a hidden gem for history lovers. Žižkov is Prague's most eccentric neighborhood with more bars per capita than almost anywhere in Europe — great for an evening if you want to extend the night.

day_by_day.morning: Letná Park & Holešovice: Take Tram 1 or 25 to Letná Park, a vast green space above the city with one of the best free panoramic views of Prague's bridges and Old Town. Visit the famous giant metronome (on the site of a former Stalin statue). Walk down into the Holešovice district — Prague's up-and-coming creative quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: DOX Centre for Contemporary Art & Farmers' Market: Visit the DOX Centre for Contemporary Art (220 CZK) — one of Central Europe's best contemporary art spaces housed in a converted factory. Afterward, browse the Holešovice Farmers' Market (Pražská tržnice) for local produce, snacks, and crafts — free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Prep & Farewell Czech Dinner: Pack your bags tonight as tomorrow you head to Budapest. Enjoy a final proper Czech dinner in Old Town. Visit a classic Czech beer hall for one last Pilsner.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh bread, local cheese, and fruit from a neighborhood grocery (Albert or Billa supermarket) — self-catered budget breakfast for ~80–100 CZK.
meals.lunch: Holešovice Farmers' Market food stalls — try traditional Czech open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky), smoked meats, or fresh pastries. Budget ~100–150 CZK.
meals.dinner: U Fleků (Křemencova 11) — Prague's most famous historic brewery (established 1499). Try their house dark lager with roast pork and dumplings. Budget ~300–400 CZK. Book ahead on Fridays as it gets busy.

day_by_day.notes: Tonight, research and confirm your Budapest transportation. The most budget-friendly option is the RegioJet or FlixBus overnight bus from Prague to Budapest (~€15–25, departs ~22:00–23:00, arrives Budapest early morning). Alternatively, a daytime train via Vienna costs more but is scenic. Book in advance for the best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Travel Day — Prague to Budapest + Arrival: Depart Prague (if taking overnight bus, you arrive in Budapest by ~08:00–09:00 at Keleti or Népliget station). Check into your Budapest accommodation (budget hostel or guesthouse in District VII — the Jewish Quarter — recommended). Freshen up and head out to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Budapest Jewish Quarter & Ruin Bars: Explore District VII (Erzsébetváros) — Budapest's vibrant Jewish Quarter. Visit the stunning Dohány Street Synagogue (exterior free, interior ~4,500 HUF / ~€12) — the largest synagogue in Europe. Wander through the neighborhood's quirky ruin bars (romkocsmák) — Szimpla Kert is the most famous and is free to enter during the day.
day_by_day.evening: Great Market Hall & Váci Street: Walk to the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — a magnificent iron-and-brick 19th-century market hall. Browse local produce, paprika, and Hungarian souvenirs. The market closes at 18:00 on Saturdays, so aim to arrive by 16:30. Stroll along the pedestrian Váci Street and along the Danube embankment as the city lights up.

meals.breakfast: On the bus/train — pack snacks from Prague the night before (bread, fruit, snacks from supermarket) to save money during transit.
meals.lunch: Karavan Street Food (Kazinczy utca 18, District VII) — an outdoor street food court next to Szimpla Kert with burgers, langos, and international food for ~1,500–2,500 HUF (~€4–7).
meals.dinner: Főzelékfaló Ételbár (Akácfa utca 9) — a beloved local Hungarian vegetable stew restaurant (főzelék) — incredibly cheap, authentic, and filling. Budget ~1,200–1,800 HUF (~€3–5). Cash preferred.

day_by_day.notes: Budapest uses Hungarian Forint (HUF). As of 2027, budget roughly 380–400 HUF per €1 (verify current rates). Withdraw HUF from an ATM (avoid dynamic currency conversion). A single metro/tram ticket costs ~450 HUF; a 24-hour pass is ~2,500 HUF — buy it at the metro station kiosk. District VII is the perfect base — walkable to most major sights.

day_by_day.morning: Buda Castle & Castle Hill: Take the M2 metro to Batthyány tér, then walk up to Castle Hill via the steep Várkert Bazár gardens (free) or take the historic Castle Funicular (~1,200 HUF one way). Explore Buda Castle (Hungarian National Gallery inside — ~2,000 HUF), the Fisherman's Bastion (free exterior, stunning neo-Gothic towers with panoramic Danube views), and Matthias Church (exterior free, interior ~2,500 HUF).
day_by_day.afternoon: Gellért Hill & Liberty Statue: Walk or take Bus 27 to Gellért Hill. Hike up to the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor) — completely free and offers the best panoramic view of Budapest, the Danube, and all seven bridges. Descend toward the Gellért Baths area and admire the Art Nouveau Gellért Hotel facade.
day_by_day.evening: Chain Bridge & Danube Promenade at Sunset: Walk across the iconic Széchenyi Chain Bridge (free) as the sun sets — the view of the illuminated Parliament building across the Danube is breathtaking. Stroll the Pest-side promenade (Duna-korzó) and enjoy the evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hold Utcai Piac (Hold utca 13, District V) — a beautiful covered market hall popular with locals on Sunday mornings. Grab fresh lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese, ~800–1,200 HUF) and a coffee.
meals.lunch: Buda Castle area — bring a packed lunch from the market or grab a sandwich from a local bakery (pékség) near Castle Hill for ~800–1,200 HUF.
meals.dinner: Menza (Liszt Ferenc tér 2) — a retro-style Hungarian bistro in a beautiful Art Nouveau square. Classic Hungarian dishes like chicken paprikash and stuffed peppers at mid-range prices. Budget ~3,500–5,000 HUF (~€9–13) with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a great day to visit Fisherman's Bastion as it's slightly less crowded in the morning. The Danube is at its most magical at sunset — don't miss the evening walk across Chain Bridge. Wear comfortable shoes — Castle Hill involves significant uphill walking on cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Hungarian Parliament Building & Kossuth Square: Take Metro M2 to Kossuth Lajos tér to see the magnificent neo-Gothic Parliament Building up close — one of the largest parliament buildings in the world. Book a guided interior tour in advance (~8,000 HUF / ~€20 for non-EU citizens, ~4,000 HUF for EU citizens) — absolutely worth it for history lovers. Explore the surrounding Kossuth Square and the Ethnographic Museum (free on Mondays).
day_by_day.afternoon: Széchenyi Thermal Baths: Head to City Park (Városliget) and spend the afternoon at the iconic Széchenyi Thermal Baths — a stunning yellow neo-Baroque building with outdoor and indoor thermal pools. Entry with locker costs ~8,000–9,000 HUF (~€21–24). A quintessential Budapest experience and perfect for tired legs after days of walking.
day_by_day.evening: Heroes' Square & City Park: After the baths, walk through City Park and visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — a grand millennium monument celebrating Hungarian history (free). In the evening, head back to the Jewish Quarter for dinner and explore the ruin bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Auguszt Cukrászda (Kossuth Lajos utca 14) — one of Budapest's oldest and most beloved pastry shops. Try rétes (Hungarian strudel) and a coffee for ~800–1,200 HUF.
meals.lunch: Govinda (Vigyázó Ferenc utca 4) — a Hare Krishna vegetarian restaurant near Parliament offering an incredibly cheap all-you-can-eat buffet for ~1,500–2,000 HUF. Beloved by budget travelers.
meals.dinner: Szimpla Kert (Kazinczy utca 14) — the original Budapest ruin bar also serves affordable food on Monday evenings (pizza, burgers, local dishes). Great atmosphere with live music sometimes. Budget ~2,000–3,000 HUF with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Book Parliament tours online at least 1–2 days in advance as they sell out quickly, especially on weekdays. The Széchenyi Baths experience is best in the late afternoon — by 16:00 the morning crowds have thinned. Bring flip-flops, a towel, and a padlock for the locker (or rent one at the baths for extra cost).

day_by_day.morning: Margaret Island (Margit-sziget): Take Tram 4 or 6 to Margit híd and walk onto Margaret Island — a beautiful car-free island in the middle of the Danube. Jog or stroll through the gardens, visit the medieval ruins of a Dominican convent and Franciscan church, see the musical fountain, and enjoy the peaceful green escape. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-Minute Sightseeing & Souvenir Shopping: Head back to the city center for any missed sights. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House (exterior free — one of Europe's most beautiful opera buildings; tours ~3,500 HUF). Browse the Váci utca shops for affordable Hungarian gifts: paprika, pálinka (fruit brandy), embroidered textiles, and Tokaji wine. Check out the Central Market Hall one more time for last-minute food souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Departure Prep: Enjoy a final Hungarian dinner before heading to the airport or train station. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Europe's most beautiful cities.

meals.breakfast: New York Café area — grab a quick coffee and croissant from a nearby bakery (~600–900 HUF) before heading to Margaret Island.
meals.lunch: Margaret Island — pack a picnic from a nearby supermarket (Lidl or Spar) with local bread, salami, cheese, and fruit for ~1,000–1,500 HUF. Eat by the fountain or in the rose garden.
meals.dinner: Borkonyhá (Sas utca 3) — a Michelin-starred wine kitchen that offers surprisingly affordable lunch-style tasting menus. For a true farewell splurge, budget ~8,000–12,000 HUF (~€21–32). Alternatively, for a budget farewell, return to Főzelékfaló for a hearty bowl of Hungarian stew (~1,500 HUF).

day_by_day.notes: If departing from Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport, take the 100E airport bus from Deák Ferenc tér (~900 HUF, ~35–40 min journey). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight. Budapest is a city that rewards slow exploration — if you have extra time on Day 8, the ruin bar district and the Danube embankment at night are unforgettable final memories.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and take the Airport Express bus or metro (Line A) to Staré Město. Journey takes approximately 45–60 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique hotel in Staré Město. Once settled, take a gentle orientation walk through Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí) to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the twin-spired Týn Church. Stroll across the nearby Charles Bridge for your first iconic Prague view over the Vltava River.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the illuminated cobblestone lanes of Staré Město as the evening crowds thin. Explore Josefov (the Jewish Quarter) from the outside, admiring its atmospheric streets. End the night with a relaxed dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on arrival — nothing formal scheduled.
meals.lunch: Café Louvre-style bistro near Old Town Square for a quick Czech open-faced sandwich (chlebíček) and soup to recharge after travel.
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved mid-range Czech gastropub serving tank-fresh Pilsner Urquell and classic svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce). Budget ~€15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Prioritize getting your bearings over cramming in sights. Book dinner reservations in advance as Lokál fills up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Old Town deep dive. Start early at Old Town Square to watch the Astronomical Clock strike the hour (best at 9:00 or 10:00 AM). Visit the Church of Our Lady before Týn, then walk through Celetná Street to the Powder Tower and Municipal House (Art Nouveau masterpiece). Climb the Powder Tower for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross Charles Bridge to Malá Strana (Lesser Town). Explore the colorful baroque streets, visit St. Nicholas Church (Malá Strana), then hike up to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad). Tour St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Allow 2.5–3 hours for the castle complex.
day_by_day.evening: Descend from the castle via Nerudova Street back into Malá Strana. Enjoy the golden-hour views from Petřín Hill lookout (take the funicular up) before heading back across the river for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy in Malá Strana — stunning Art Nouveau interior, excellent Czech pastries and eggs. Budget ~€10–12.
meals.lunch: Malá Strana street food or a quick bite at one of the castle-area cafés — try trdelník (chimney cake) or a light soup bowl.
meals.dinner: Eska — a celebrated farm-to-table Czech restaurant in Karlín (short tram ride). Modern Czech cuisine with seasonal ingredients. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is one of the largest castle complexes in the world — wear comfortable shoes. Buy castle tickets online in advance to skip queues. Petřín funicular runs until 23:30.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Josefov — Prague's historic Jewish Quarter. Visit the Jewish Museum complex, which includes the Old Jewish Cemetery, Pinkas Synagogue (Holocaust memorial), and the Spanish Synagogue (stunning Moorish interior). This is one of the most moving cultural experiences in Central Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods by tram for a local, non-touristy Prague experience. Browse the Náměstí Míru square, peek into Art Nouveau apartment buildings, and visit the quirky Žižkov Television Tower (with David Černý's crawling baby sculptures). Explore the Olšany Cemetery for a contemplative walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Staré Město for a final Prague evening. Walk along the Vltava riverside promenade at sunset, then enjoy a Czech beer tasting at a traditional pivnice (pub).

meals.breakfast: Your hotel or a nearby bakery — try koláče (Czech pastries filled with poppy seed or jam).
meals.lunch: Nase Maso — a beloved local butcher-deli in Staré Město serving outstanding Czech sandwiches and meatballs. Very affordable, ~€8–10.
meals.dinner: Kantýna — upscale butcher-restaurant concept in Prague 1, excellent Czech steaks and grilled meats. Budget ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Jewish Museum tickets must be purchased in advance — availability is limited and it sells out. Closed on Saturdays and Jewish holidays. Allow at least 2–2.5 hours for the full complex.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Prague to Budapest by train. Take the scenic Railjet or EuroCity train from Praha Hlavní Nádraží (Prague Main Station) — journey is approximately 6.5–7 hours with beautiful countryside views through Bohemia, Austria/Slovakia border regions. Trains depart around 7:00–9:00 AM; book in advance on Czech Railways (ČD) or Railjet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest Keleti or Kelenföld station in the early-to-mid afternoon. Transfer to your Budapest accommodation. Take a gentle first walk along the Danube riverbank — the view of Buda Castle and the Chain Bridge from the Pest side is immediately breathtaking. Stroll up to the Fisherman's Bastion in Buda for golden-hour panoramas over the city.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Castle District (Várhegy) in Buda as the evening lights come on. Visit Matthias Church exterior, then descend to the Chain Bridge and cross to the Pest side for dinner in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at your Prague hotel or grab pastries and coffee at the train station before departure.
meals.lunch: Train dining car or packed food from a Prague deli — enjoy the scenic journey through Central Europe.
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen — a Michelin-recommended Budapest restaurant with excellent Hungarian wine pairings and modern Hungarian cuisine. Budget ~€25–35 per person. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance for best prices and seat availability. The train journey itself is a highlight — sit on the left side for the best river views entering Budapest. Consider a 2nd class Railjet seat for comfort at mid-range budget.

day_by_day.morning: Full Budapest Castle District morning. Revisit Fisherman's Bastion in daylight for the best Danube panoramas. Tour Matthias Church interior (stunning neo-Gothic with Hungarian folk art motifs). Walk through the historic Castle District streets to the Budapest History Museum and the Royal Palace complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Chain Bridge back to Pest. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings) — book a guided interior tour in advance. Walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) to Vörösmarty Square, then explore the elegant Váci Street shopping corridor.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's famous ruin bar scene in the Jewish Quarter (VII District). Start at Szimpla Kert — the original and most iconic ruin bar — for drinks and the eclectic atmosphere. The area around Kazinczy Street is full of bars, street food, and live music on weekends.

meals.breakfast: New York Café — one of the world's most beautiful cafés, serving Hungarian breakfast in an opulent gilded interior. A splurge worth having (~€15–18). Or opt for a nearby bakery for budget ~€5–7.
meals.lunch: Central Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) — Budapest's stunning 19th-century iron-and-brick market. Try lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) and browse local produce. Budget ~€6–10.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Kazinczy Street restaurant before the ruin bar evening — Macesz Huszár for traditional Jewish-Hungarian cuisine in the heart of the old Jewish Quarter. Budget ~€18–25.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be pre-booked online at the official website. Saturday evenings in the ruin bar district are very lively — arrive at Szimpla Kert before 9 PM to get a good spot. The Jewish Quarter is safe and walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Budapest thermal bath experience — visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath in City Park (the largest medicinal bath in Europe, housed in a stunning neo-baroque yellow palace). Spend 2–3 hours soaking in the outdoor and indoor thermal pools. A quintessential Budapest experience. Budget ~€20–25 entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) adjacent to Széchenyi — visit Vajdahunyad Castle (a fairy-tale complex of architectural styles), and stroll through the park. Then head to Andrássy Avenue, Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard, and visit the House of Terror Museum — a powerful and sobering museum documenting Hungary's Nazi and Soviet occupation periods.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube — a 1–1.5 hour evening boat tour offers spectacular illuminated views of the Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, and bridges. One of the most memorable experiences in Budapest. Book in advance (~€15–20).

meals.breakfast: Café near your accommodation or a local pékség (bakery) for fresh kifli (crescent rolls) and coffee — very local and affordable (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Gundel Restaurant garden café (near City Park) for a lighter Hungarian lunch — goulash soup and a main. Mid-range lunch ~€18–22.
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown — Budapest's celebrated fine-dining restaurant with a Michelin star, offering modern Hungarian tasting menus. A special evening splurge (~€45–60 per person). Alternatively, Menza on Liszt Ferenc Square for excellent modern Hungarian at ~€20–28.

day_by_day.notes: Széchenyi is busiest on weekends — arrive early (opens 6 AM) or after 2 PM to avoid peak crowds. Bring a towel or rent one on-site. The House of Terror is closed Mondays. Book the Danube cruise at least a day ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Szentendre — a charming artists' village 40 minutes north of Budapest by HÉV suburban railway (Line H5 from Batthyány tér). Explore the colorful Serbian baroque architecture, Orthodox churches, and art galleries. Visit the Hungarian Open Air Museum (Skanzen) — an outstanding open-air folk museum showing traditional Hungarian village life across different regions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Szentendre's cobblestone streets. Browse local craft shops, galleries, and the famous Marzipan Museum. Return to Budapest by late afternoon via HÉV. Back in the city, explore the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street — the largest synagogue in Europe and a deeply moving site.
day_by_day.evening: Final Budapest evening — head to the Buda side and climb Gellért Hill to the Citadella for a spectacular panoramic night view over the entire city, the Danube, and all seven bridges. A perfect farewell to Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick café stop before catching the HÉV train.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Szentendre — Rab Ráby restaurant for traditional Hungarian home cooking in a historic setting. Budget ~€14–18.
meals.dinner: Gellért Hill area or back in central Pest — Rosenstein Restaurant for Hungarian Jewish cuisine, a family-run institution beloved by locals. Budget ~€20–28.

day_by_day.notes: HÉV trains to Szentendre run every 10–20 minutes from Batthyány tér metro station. Use your Budapest public transport card. The Great Synagogue is closed Saturdays — Monday is perfect. Gellért Hill is a 20–30 minute uphill walk or take bus 27.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — depending on your departure time, visit any missed highlights. Consider the Hungarian National Museum for a comprehensive overview of Hungarian history, or browse the Fény utca Market for local produce, spices, and paprika to bring home as souvenirs. Walk along the Danube one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport. Allow 60–90 minutes for the journey (Bus 100E direct from Deák Ferenc tér, or taxi/rideshare ~€20–25). Check in and depart.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — end of your 8-day Prague & Budapest adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast — try a traditional rakott krumpli (layered potato casserole) or eggs and langos at a local café near your hotel.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a quick stop at a central Budapest café before heading to the airport.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at your destination.

day_by_day.notes: Budapest Airport is approximately 30 km from the city center. Bus 100E is the most convenient and affordable option (~€3). Allow extra time on departure day for any last-minute souvenir shopping at the Central Market Hall if it's on your route. Keep some Hungarian forints (HUF) for the bus or small purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged to boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Staré Město. Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge, admire the Baroque statues, and take in your first views of Prague Castle across the Vltava River. Explore the winding cobblestone lanes of the Old Town at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium Old Town restaurant. Visit the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) at dusk for a magical first impression of Old Town Square, beautifully lit in the early evening. End the night with a glass of Moravian wine at a rooftop bar overlooking the city.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel or a nearby café such as Café Savoy-style brasserie near the hotel
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — Michelin-starred Czech tasting menu in the heart of Old Town, showcasing elevated traditional Bohemian cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private luxury transfer from Václav Havel Airport in advance. Day 1 is intentionally light to allow for jet lag recovery and gentle acclimatization. Ask the hotel concierge to book Day 2–3 restaurant reservations upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Prague Castle complex — explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane. Arrive early to beat the crowds and enjoy panoramic views over the red rooftops of Prague.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) and explore the charming baroque district. Visit the exquisite Wallenstein Garden and the Church of St. Nicholas. Cross back over Charles Bridge and spend time browsing the antique galleries and artisan boutiques of Staré Město.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical concert — Prague is renowned for intimate evening performances in historic venues. Choose a Mozart or Dvořák concert held inside a baroque palace or church in Old Town. Follow with a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a full spread with fresh pastries, cold cuts, and Czech cheeses
meals.lunch: Terasa U Zlaté Studně — rooftop restaurant in Malá Strana with panoramic castle views and refined Czech-European cuisine
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant — creative contemporary Czech cuisine using seasonal local ingredients, located in Old Town

day_by_day.notes: Book the Prague Castle private guide in advance through the hotel concierge. Evening concert tickets should be secured ahead of time — the Municipal House or a baroque palace venue is recommended for an authentic premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of the best-preserved Jewish historical districts in Europe. Tour the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Old-New Synagogue (Europe's oldest active synagogue), and the Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting memorial walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Prague Museum of Decorative Arts and the Agnes Convent for a deep dive into medieval Bohemian art. Afterward, take a private 1-hour Vltava River cruise on a luxury boat for a unique perspective of the city's bridges and skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Vinohrady neighborhood for dinner — a slightly more local, upscale district beloved by Prague's creative class. Return to Old Town for a nightcap at a sophisticated cocktail bar.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá — celebrated Czech gastropub serving perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell tank beer and elevated traditional dishes like svíčková and roast duck
meals.dinner: Eska — acclaimed modern Czech restaurant in Karlín blending fermentation, wood-fire cooking, and seasonal local produce

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter entrance requires a combined ticket — purchase in advance online to skip queues. The Vltava cruise can be arranged as a private charter through the hotel for a truly premium experience. September weather is typically mild and pleasant — ideal for river cruising.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora — a UNESCO World Heritage Site just 1.5 hours from Prague. Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), decorated entirely with human bones, and the stunning Gothic Cathedral of St. Barbara, one of the finest Gothic churches in Central Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kutná Hora's medieval silver-mining heritage at the Czech Museum of Silver, then wander the beautifully preserved historic town center. Private car returns you to Prague in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Prague. Enjoy a leisurely evening in Staré Město — browse the upscale boutiques along Pařížská Street (Prague's luxury shopping avenue) before a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Dačický Restaurant in Kutná Hora — charming medieval-style restaurant serving hearty Bohemian cuisine in a historic setting
meals.dinner: Alcron Restaurant — elegant Art Deco seafood restaurant in Prague, one of the city's most celebrated fine-dining establishments

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private chauffeured car for the Kutná Hora day trip — far more comfortable than the train and allows flexible timing. The Ossuary is a genuinely unique cultural experience unlike anywhere else in Europe. Book dinner at Alcron well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic luxury train or private car transfer from Prague to Budapest (approximately 7 hours by train — book a first-class compartment on the EuroCity service, or opt for a private chauffeured car for ultimate flexibility). Depart mid-morning to arrive in Budapest by early evening.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest and check into your luxury hotel in the Pest city center (recommended: Matild Palace, Anantara New York Palace, or Four Seasons Gresham Palace). Freshen up and take a first walk along the Danube Promenade at golden hour.
day_by_day.evening: First dinner in Budapest at a celebrated restaurant near your hotel. Walk along the illuminated Chain Bridge and admire the stunning Parliament Building lit up across the river — one of Europe's most spectacular urban night views.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast in Prague before departure
meals.lunch: First-class dining car on the EuroCity train, or a picnic of premium Czech provisions prepared by your Prague hotel
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown — Budapest's Michelin-starred restaurant offering innovative Hungarian-European cuisine in a stylish setting

day_by_day.notes: The Prague–Budapest journey is part of the experience — a first-class train compartment through the Bohemian and Slovak countryside is scenic and memorable. Alternatively, a private luxury transfer can be arranged. Confirm Budapest hotel check-in time in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Buda Castle District — explore the Royal Palace, Matthias Church, and the Fisherman's Bastion with its fairy-tale turrets and sweeping panoramic views over the Danube and Pest. Discover the medieval streets of Castle Hill at a relaxed premium pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Chain Bridge and explore the grand boulevards of Pest. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (one of the largest in the world) on a private guided interior tour. Walk along Andrássy Avenue, Budapest's Champs-Élysées, lined with neo-Renaissance mansions and luxury boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Hungarian thermal bath ritual at Széchenyi or Gellért Baths — book a private evening session for an exclusive, uncrowded experience. Follow with a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Halászbástya Restaurant at the Fisherman's Bastion — panoramic terrace dining with Hungarian specialties and Danube views
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant — two Michelin-starred Hungarian fine dining in the heart of Budapest, offering an extraordinary tasting menu of reimagined Magyar classics

day_by_day.notes: Book the Parliament interior tour in advance as slots fill quickly, especially on weekends. A private thermal bath booking through your hotel concierge ensures a serene, exclusive experience away from the weekend crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's stunning 19th-century iron market hall. Browse premium Hungarian products including Tokaji wine, foie gras, paprika, salami, and artisan crafts. Excellent for premium gift shopping and local food discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jewish Quarter and the magnificent Dohány Street Synagogue — the largest synagogue in Europe and a deeply moving cultural landmark. Visit the adjacent Jewish Museum and the poignant Raoul Wallenberg Memorial Park. Stroll through the trendy ruin bar district of the 7th district.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Danube river cruise on a private luxury boat — champagne on board as you glide past the illuminated Parliament, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge. This is widely considered one of the most beautiful urban river views in the world. Dinner at a celebrated restaurant afterward.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Borkonyha Winekitchen — Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant specializing in Hungarian wines paired with seasonal modern cuisine
meals.dinner: Stand Restaurant — Michelin-starred, helmed by celebrated chef Szabina Szulló and Tamás Széll, showcasing the very best of contemporary Hungarian gastronomy

day_by_day.notes: The private Danube evening cruise is the highlight of Budapest and should be booked well in advance through your hotel. September evenings are warm enough to enjoy the open deck. The Great Market Hall is at its best in the morning before tour groups arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Museum of Fine Arts, home to an outstanding collection of European masters. Alternatively, explore the serene Margaret Island in the middle of the Danube — a green oasis perfect for a peaceful morning stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping along Váci Street or Andrássy Avenue. Visit a premium Hungarian wine shop to stock up on world-class Tokaji Aszú and Egri Bikavér wines. Return to hotel for final packing and checkout. Private transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on an extraordinary 8-day journey through two of Europe's most magnificent capital cities.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the hotel — request a full Hungarian breakfast with fresh lángos, cold cuts, local cheeses, and Hungarian pastries
meals.lunch: New York Café — one of the most beautiful cafés in the world, housed in the opulent New York Palace. A perfect final Budapest lunch experience
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight, depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for the airport transfer and check-in. Ask your hotel concierge to arrange a private luxury transfer. Consider purchasing a curated Hungarian gift hamper (wine, paprika, foie gras) from the hotel or a specialist deli as a premium souvenir of the trip.
